claims.text: The target material class is multicomponent high-entropy alloys containing five or more principal elements.
The method is intended to treat both solid and liquid alloy states.
The relevant states are at or near the alloys' high melting temperatures.
Conventional EAM references do not adequately represent the broad configurational diversity of ab initio liquids.
The limitations of EAM references produce relatively large thermodynamic-integration path mismatches in TOR-TILD.
An MLIP should be trained on an extensive ab initio dataset spanning high-temperature solid and liquid configurations and used in place of the EAM reference.
Training on diverse solid and liquid configurations will make the MLIP potential-energy surface more closely match the ab initio potential-energy surface.
The closer potential-energy-surface match will cause the reference system to sample the target system's phase space more completely.
An MLIP trained on both phases will capture subtle configurational variations that EAM potentials miss.
Improved reference-target phase-space overlap will shorten the thermodynamic-integration path and reduce integration errors.
Replacing TOR-TILD's EAM references with the MLIP will reduce path mismatch by approximately one order of magnitude.
The reduced path mismatch will yield more accurate free-energy calculations.
The proposed intervention is applicable within approximately plus or minus 10–20% of the melting temperature.
The intervention should work best for alloys with at least five metallic elements near their melting temperatures.
Its applicability to alloys with fewer components or to systems far from high-temperature conditions is uncertain.
The magnitude of improvement depends on the quality and representativeness of the ab initio training database.
Additional elemental and binary-system benchmarks are needed to refine the predicted improvement.
